we introduce SRE-Bench, the first realistic, contamination-free RE benchmark.
Built entirely from scratch by RE experts with over 5,000 expert hours, SRE-Bench comprises 19 private, real-world-scale programs averaging 16.9K lines of code.
We further developed 44 in-house anti-analysis mechanisms, yielding 262 binary instances and 1,572 deterministically graded tasks.
GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Fable-5.1, despite their strong source-code cybersecurity capabilities, fully solve only 31.5% and 26.9% of graded instances, respectively.
This result suggests that success in source-code security does not necessarily translate into effective binary analysis.

Third, we present SRE-Bench, the first RE benchmark that addresses both requirements: 262 instances built from scratch at the real-world scale (averaging 16,915.8 LoC), paired with a 27K-LoC anti-analysis suite implementing 44 in-house protection primitives.

SRE-Bench contains 262 instances, spanning five domains that together cover the breadth of real-world RE practice (Kabir et al., 2026; Eilam, 2011): network protocol, game, format parser, malware, and firmware.
It provides 44 distinct protection primitives organized into nine technique families.
To our knowledge, more than half of these primitives, primarily in families (3), (4), (7), (9), and (8), have no publicly available implementations.
We compile each of the 19 programs and, where applicable, harden it with the suite, yielding 262 binary instances.

For each of the 16 programs in the four domains (i.e., network protocol, game, format parser, malware), we build 8 unprotected instances that cover all combinations across three compilation axes (i.e., optimization, symbol stripping, and static vs. dynamic linking) plus 8 protected instances
In total, SRE-Bench provides 1,572 RE tasks.
In total, SRE-Bench comprises over 320K lines of code (Table 2), averaging 16,915.8 LoC per program; it is 30-470× larger than prior RE benchmarks.

Each runs inside a standardized mini-SWE-agent, so that differences in scaffolding do not confound the comparison. Every model is queried at its highest reasoning-effort setting, and each run is capped at 500 model steps and 6 hours of wall-clock time.

The Unconstrained setting (Figure 4) evaluated three OpenAI models and two Anthropic models at the providers’ default settings, using Codex for OpenAI models and Claude Code for Anthropic models, without cyber safeguards and evaluation budget limits.
This internal evaluation comprises 16,768 attempts and 2.37B output tokens, corresponding to a token-equivalent cost of roughly $566,000 (Table 8).
Grader code, reference solutions, and any development artifacts are removed from the container, and agents receive no scoring feedback during a run.
All averages are computed over gradable runs, excluding cyber guardrail refusals and failures due to limited context window.

For the unconstrained evaluation, we report pass@1 and pass@4 from n = 4 attempts per instance using the unbiased estimator of Chen et al. (2021), under which pass@1 is the mean full-solve rate across attempts and pass@4 the fraction of instances solved by at least one attempt.
#Graded is the number of runs that produced a gradable result; the remainder failed either due to guarded-model refusal or context-window limits
Only graded instances are used to compute the metrics.
In contrast, GPT-6-Astra leads on SRE-Bench, averaging 5.55 out of 6 and fully solving 149 of 181 gradable instances (82.3%); only 3.9% of gradable instances receive no credit.
Although the tasks are not exploitation-oriented, frequent refusals on cyber safety grounds leave GPT-6-Astra with the fewest gradable instances (181 of 262, 69.1%) in the public setting.
All these scores are conditional on a gradable result and should not be interpreted as success rates over all 262 instances.

GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Fable-5.1, despite their strong source-code security capabilities (OpenAI, 2026a; Anthropic, 2026a), fully solve only 80/254 (31.5%) and 60/223 (26.9%) graded instances, respectively, with mean scores of 3.69 and 2.58 out of 6.
These results reinforce the need to evaluate binary analysis as a distinct capability rather than infer it from success on source-code security tasks.
Hardening cuts GPT-5.6-sol’s score from 4.69 to 2.50 and reduces every other model besides GPT-6-Astra to at most 0.33.
Claude-Fable-5.1 falls from 5.33, second only to GPT-6-Astra without hardening, to 0.32
GPT-6-Astra, by contrast, unpacks consistently and loses only 0.10 points.
However, analyzing protection increases its cost, at 1.5× the dollars per point of unpacked instances, versus 3.4× for GPT-5.6-sol and 9–35× for weaker models (Table 7).

High pass@4 means the private grader finds a correct solution among four attempts; practical use requires choosing or validating one without that grader.
For GPT-6-Astra, 69 instances have both successful and unsuccessful attempts, and 126 of its 1,048 attempts fail to obtain full credit.
SRE-Bench is built from 19 programs. This is a small pool in absolute terms.
To remain contamination-free, every target program, its evaluation infrastructure, and the protection layer must be developed from scratch; doing so required more than 5,000 expert hours.
Despite the limited program count, SRE-Bench contains over 320K lines of authored code, averaging 16,915.8 LoC per program, together with a 27K-LoC protection suite.
These programs produce 1,572 deterministically scored tasks.
This scale is already sufficient to expose large capability differences: across the eight public models, mean scores differ by more than 25×.
Our programs average 16,915.8 LoC and thus do not cover the largest real-world software systems, which can reach hundreds of thousands or millions of lines of code.
Nevertheless, our programs are already 30–470× larger than those used in prior RE benchmarks.
We presented SRE-Bench, the first RE benchmark that is at once contamination-free and built at real-world scale.
Fable-5.1 fully solve only 31.5% and 26.9% of graded instances, and our anti-analysis suite halves the former while reducing every weaker model to near zero.
a program derived from public code can be recovered for roughly $2 in ten minutes, while small clean-room programs are solved nearly perfectly
To preserve the contamination resistance of SRE-Bench, we do not publicly release the benchmark binaries or task instances.

Instead, we provide an open evaluation service through which researchers can request evaluation of their models or agents; we run the experiments in the same controlled environment and report the resulting metrics.
To reduce risks to real systems, the benchmark is constructed from programs developed in-house rather than vulnerabilities or binaries collected from deployed third-party software.
Experiments are conducted in isolated environments, and the benchmark does not require interaction with external systems or services.

The agent receives a client binary that implements a proprietary, encrypted client–server protocol, together with a handful of partial packet captures that mimic the limited network traces available to analysts in practice. No specification is provided.
A live server grades that driver over a single metered TCP connection, capped at 64 messages, scoring how deep into the protocol’s state space the agent can legally drive
The target is a fully playable, 20-floor terminal roguelike featuring combat, spellcasting, crafting, shops, factions, quests, and achievements.

Hidden within the binary are six behaviors that never arise during normal play and are not documented in the manual; each is triggered silently by conditions that can be identified only by reconstructing the relevant program logic.

It is distributed as an encoder only: the binary contains no decompressor, so the agent must reverse engineer the multi-stage encoding pipeline and implement a decoder that reconstructs the original files byte-for-byte.
The target is a malware-themed Linux implant that is inert and safe by construction.
The task is defensive: the agent must understand the implant well enough to implement a cleanup tool that surgically removes each family’s artifacts while preserving grader-planted benign data.
Instance-specific names, paths, and keys are all derived from a fresh secret on each run to prevent hard-coded cleanup strategies.

The agent interacts with the device only through a JTAG-style interface to a from-scratch emulator that models the chip’s memory map, peripherals, and serial command interface, subject to a per-session budget of 5,000 commands.

The six scored anchors form a capability ladder: (1) recover the framing and complete the cryptographic handshake; (2) reconstruct the capability-tier state machine and forge the promotion tokens that gate the top tier
Every preset shares a common baseline – per-page authenticated encryption, fold-not-branch keying, self-checksumming, loader virtualization, and the obfuscation and stripping layers
GPT-6-Astra is largely unaffected, scoring between 5.25 and 6.00 on every preset.

GPT-5.6-sol is the only other model that retains non-trivial capability, scoring between 1.93 and 3.19; every remaining model stays below 0.6 on every preset, and GLM-5.2 scores exactly 0.00 on all eight.
